messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@carvoyant.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@carvoyant.com
Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Seasonal SLA add-on & escalation credits — details?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ramping into our seasonal window (late Q3 -> Q4) and need clarity on how Redwood would support a predictable surge: specifically, an "escalation credit" model (prepaid incident credits that can be redeemed for faster on-call response + engineering triage), plus a short-term seasonal SLA add-on for burst capacity.

Can you send the packaging options (what's included in each band), the pricing per-credit, and any minimum commit/term you require for seasonal add-on? A couple of constraints from finance/procurement:
- We prefer a prepaid block vs per-incident billing.
- Need an option that includes a guaranteed 2-hour initial response for critical incidents.
- Any rate card changes for timezone-covered support (we operate PST with some EU overlap)

Attached is our internal incident-runbook excerpt (for context). If you can get a quick matrix over today or tomorrow that'd be great — I'll loop procurement once I have numbers.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Head of Operations — Carvoyant
Attachments: carvoyant-runbook-excerpt.docx (stub)

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@carvoyant.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA add-on & escalation credits — details?

Hi Lina — great to hear from you and congrats on the ramp. Below is a compact set of options we typically offer for seasonal surges; I attached a concise SLA matrix (sample-sla-matrix.xlsx) and the escalation playbook PDF.

Packaging (ballpark):
1) Standard (no additional charge) — 24/7 support triage, standard queue, 8 business-hour response for P1. No prepaid credits.
2) Premium Escalation Pack — 99.95% availability, guaranteed 2-hour response for P1, includes 10 escalation credits/month (credits use: on-call escalation + engineering triage, 1 credit ≈ one 1-hour escalated triage). Pricing: $6k–$9k/mo depending on commit.
3) Seasonal Add-on (prepaid blocks) — 25/50/100-credit blocks for short windows (1–3 months). Blocks are discounted vs ad-hoc by ~15–30% depending on upfront commit. Example: 50 credits prepaid ≈ $8k (net), refundable as credit toward support next 12 months if unused.

Key terms and notes:
- We can offer a one-time onboarding discount (15–20%) for the first seasonal period if Carvoyant commits to a minimum 3-month add-on.
- Geography: PST coverage is included; we can add a European overlap window (+5% premium) if you want guaranteed EU daytime triage.
- Billing: prepaid blocks invoiced up-front; unused credits can roll to a 12-mo credit balance (or be refunded pro-rata on annual conversion).

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the matrix and pick the right block size. If you prefer, I can send a draft quote and DocuSign link after we land the qty/term.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample-sla-matrix.xlsx (stub), redwood-escalation-playbook.pdf (stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Seasonal SLA add-on & escalation credits — Carvoyant (pricing ask)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Carvoyant's ask (see original thread below). Quick summary of the numbers I'm proposing to keep the deal moving:
- Offer: 50-credit Seasonal Add-on block for the initial Q3->Q4 window
- List price guidance: $9,500 for 50 credits (list)
- Negotiation target: provide 18% upfront discount -> $7,790
- Premium Escalation Pack monthly (if they go full premium): $7k/mo (at our mid-commit tier)

Asking approvals:
1) I want flexibility to go to 20% on onboarding discount for first year to close.
2) Approve leaving escalation-credit price at $250/credit floor for renewals (we can discount the initial block more aggressively).

Rationale: retail seasonality leads to high marginal value for quick triage; Carvoyant is a mid-sized account with potential to expand to Dedicated capacity next year. If we push too little on discount they'll shop; if we push too much we compress expansion economics.

Can you advise the acceptable range? If OK I will send a draft quote + proposed DocuSign with a 3-month seasonal term and rollover terms.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom — thanks for the quick summary. I'm comfortable approving a promotional onboarding discount up to 18% for the first seasonal period. Conditions:

- No deeper stackable discounts beyond onboarding (i.e., no both deeper onboarding + volume discount in year 1).
- Require legal to add a "seasonal term" clause: commits only cover the stated period (3 months) and credits roll to a 12-month balance if unused.
